## **Naggaroth Land of Chill**
Gemstones and precious metals are found in abundance, mined by thralls on behalf of the most privileged highborn, who are granted fiefdoms by Malerion when they prove loyal and useful to him. 

## **Naggaroth**
Naggaroth, which means Land of Chill in the Druchii tongue, became a refuge for Malerion and his followers after the Sundering. The refugees of lost Nagarythe found themselves on the shores of a bleak, windswept, and foreboding continent few had visited before their arrival. For now, and for the foreseeable future, it would be both their home and a cradle for the nurturing of a slow but dreadful revenge against Ulthuan. Though the dark elves dominate Naggaroth, it is often as dangerous to them as any enemy from the Chaos Wastes or across the seas. 

## **Warped Timber**
a shipment of exotic timber is offered for sale at the importExport Exchange in Marienburg. Several merchant houses offer a princely sum, as the dark-hued wood is lightweight yet harder than steel. the stevedore Jens Korf handled the cargo, and for the last week has suffered nightmares and waking visions of pain, hearing whispers in a cruel tongue. the merchant who acquired the timber wants agents to discreetly trace the wood’s origin and cleanse the curse before their buyers discover it. the wood came from Norscan traders, who stole it from a dark elf ship they attacked in the great ocean. it is haunted by the souls of captive wretches who died in the forests of Naggaroth. 

A vast continent, Naggaroth extends into the far north, where the Ironfrost Glacier and northern watchtowers form a frontier with the nightmare realms of the Chaos Wastes. South of the towers, the tundra and mountains are barren of all but the hardiest plants and animals, trees that hug the ground closely against the ever-blowing winds, wiry grasses, sickly lichens clinging to the rocks, and herds of wild, shaggy bison that feed on them. Many of the rivers that water these lands flow from the northern wastes, polluted with their poisonous energies. 

Malerion’s focus is always on Ulthuan, so for centuries, his people explored little of the far west. The terrain was hostile and, after the loss of expeditions sent to find a route to the Far Sea, few dared to venture there. Raids were confined to the Sea of Chaos and the Great Ocean, and the dark elves sought a western passage to plunder the lands of the far east. The search finally ended when Lord Maglen of Hag Graef sailed his scout ship into a vast, uncharted cavern. As he explored, he found a labyrinthe of dark tunnels, that he callrd the Underworld Sea. 

Further south is Malerion’s dark empire, its cities clinging to a narrow band around the shores of the Sea of Malice and the Sea of Chill. Often wracked by raging storms or choked by hazardous icebergs, the Druchii’s sleek ships and black arks sail these seas like nobility taking a stroll in their gardens, bringing cargoes of captives and treasures back to Naggaroth. Malerion’s captains have mastered these waters and can use their hazards as weapons against any who dare to pursue them. 

These waters remain largely uncharted, but ships that brave the many hazards can reach the Boiling Sea, where sea monsters lurk amongst scattered islands. Tamed by Druchii beastmasters, these have become both beasts of burden and nearly unstoppable living weapons to use against the enemy. The caverns of the Underworld Sea are large enough for a black ark to pass through, allowing them to raid the lands of Grand Cathay, the coasts of Khuresh, and the Lost Isles of Elithis. 

After the Sundering, sorcerers grounded several arks, merging them with the shores of their new realm to found Naggaroth’s cities. West and north of the cities are barely fertile lands, jagged mountains, rugged valleys, and vast forests of dark timber. To the south is the inhospitable waste of the Ironsand Desert, and the peaks of the Titan and Grey Guardian mountain chains. These serve as an inaccessible bulwark against incursions by the cold-blooded inhabitants of Lustria. 

## **Warmer Waters**
duriath helbane has heard tell of a migration of sea dragons abandoning Naggaroth’s west coast, appearing in the waters off Lustria’s isthmus. Such a gathering could prove fruitful for his corsairs, either to test their mettle or to find and collect fresh eggs. The fleetmaster allows each ship setting out to ensnare a sea dragon to take a complement of prisoners, such as the Characters, to act as bait. 

Though a harsh land, Naggaroth holds riches for those willing to defy it. The forests provide some of the finest timber in the world, felled by forced labour to make more ships to bring their masters more captives.

## **Malerion, Society, and Religion**
_’That realm should have consumed itself long ago. That it hasn’t is a testament to one thing alone: Malerion’s iron will.’_ 

— Banadil Anwelior, Asur Spy 

In the paranoid and cruel society of the dark elves, one individual is vaunted above all others. Malerion sits at the summit of the hierarchy, ruling from his chambers atop the highest tower in his city of Naggarond. Son and self-proclaimed rightful heir of Aenarion, everyone else in Naggaroth, living, dead, or otherwise, exists to serve him. Malerion’s rule, while absolute and unimaginably brutal, is not quite totalitarian. He grants the cities a degree of self-determination, appointing _drachau_ as rulers of Naggaroth’s six great cities. These highest of the highborn scheme and conspire against one another for wealth, power, and Malerion’s favour. 

The Dread King cultivates rivalries at all levels of Naggaroth’s society. His subjects are too busy plotting against each other to rise against him, and the regular turmoil and upheaval serves to weed out the weak, so those strong enough to survive are likely to be strong enough to challenge Ulthuan. To this end, Malerion dominates all and eliminates those he deems unworthy. Only Morathi and Crone Hellebron of Khaine’s cult come close to his level of authority, and even they know there are limits. 

Religion is the other force that pervades Druchii society, as even Malerion is a devotee to the Cytharai, the gods of the Underworld. All are worshipped in Naggaroth, though Khaine, Lord of Murder, is supreme. Centred on his great temple in Har Ganeth, the cult’s insatiable demand for sacrificial blood drives overseas expeditions almost as much as the need for fresh labour in Naggaroth. A lust for murder and death reaches all levels of Druchii society, and once a year, on Death Night, the witch elves may slay in Khaine’s name anyone they find on the street or in the homes they force an entry into.
